questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Value of a Parameter that Results in Resonance
questions.problem:
The position $y(t),$ measured in meters, of a particle oscillating with periodically forced harmonic motion without damping is governed by the equation

$$
{y}^{″}+6y=\operatorname{cos}⁡pt+\operatorname{sin}⁡pt,
$$

where $t>0$ is the time, in seconds. Which value of the parameter $p$ causes the oscillator to resonate?
questions.worked_solution:
The equation of forced harmonic motion without damping is

$$
{y}^{″}+{\omega }^{2}y=f(t).
$$

The complementary solution ${y}_{c}$ here represents simple harmonic motion, and it can be written as

$$
{y}_{c}=A\operatorname{cos}⁡\omega t+B\operatorname{sin}⁡\omega t,
$$

where $A$ and $B$ are arbitrary constants of integration.

In our case,

$$
{\omega }^{2}=6\,⟹\,\omega =\sqrt{6}.
$$

Thus, we have

$$
{y}_{c}=A\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{6}t+B\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{6}t.
$$

The oscillator experiences resonance when the frequency $p$ of the external periodic force $f(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡pt+\operatorname{sin}⁡pt$ coincides with the frequency of the complementary solution, which is $\omega =\sqrt{6}.$

Therefore, the oscillator experiences resonance when $p=\sqrt{6}.$

questions.problem:
A particle of mass $0.8\,\text{kg}$ is attached to a massless spring. An external periodic force $F(t)=2cos\,(\frac{5}{2}t)\,\text{N}$ is applied to the particle.

The position of the particle is $y(t)$ (measured in meters), and $t>0$ is the time in seconds. If the particle moves with forced harmonic motion without damping and the system experiences resonance, what is the spring constant $k?$

$k=$
{{field-1}}${\text{kg/s}}^{2}$
questions.worked_solution:
The equation of motion for a particle of mass $m$ moving with forced harmonic motion without damping under the action of a spring with spring constant $k$ and external force $F(t)$ is given by

$$
m{y}^{″}=-ky+F(t).
$$

Substituting our values for $m$ and $F(t)$ gives

$$
0.8{y}^{″}=-ky+2cos\,(\frac{5}{2}t).
$$

Simplifying and rearranging the above equation, we get

$$
{y}^{″}+\frac{5k}{4}y=\frac{5}{2}cos\,(\frac{5}{2}t).
$$

The complementary solution ${y}_{c}$ here represents simple harmonic motion, and it can be written as

$$
{y}_{c}=A\operatorname{cos}⁡\omega t+B\operatorname{sin}⁡\omega t,
$$

where $A$ and $B$ are arbitrary constants of integration, and $\omega $ is the system's internal frequency.

In our case,

$$
{\omega }^{2}=\frac{5k}{4}\,⟹\,k=\frac{4}{5}{\omega }^{2}.
$$

The oscillator experiences resonance when the frequency of the external periodic force $f(t)=\frac{5}{2}cos\,(\frac{5}{2}t),$ which is $\frac{5}{2},$ is equal to the frequency of the complementary solution $\omega .$

Therefore,

$$
k=\frac{4}{5}{\omega }^{2}=\frac{4}{5}\cdot {(\frac{5}{2})}^{2}=5\,{\text{kg/s}}^{2}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Identifying Solutions to Forced Harmonic Motion Equations
questions.problem:
A particle is moving with forced harmonic motion without damping. The particle is acted on by an external periodic force
$f(t)=-12\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-3\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t).$
Assuming the system experiences resonance, which of the following could be used to represent the general solution for the position $y(t)?$

- $y=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t+ϕ)+\frac{1}{2}t\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-2t\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)$
- $y=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t+ϕ)+\frac{1}{2}t\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-2t\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)$
- $y=A\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)+\frac{1}{2}t\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-2t\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)$

Note that $A,$ $B,$ $R,$ and $ϕ$ are constants.
questions.worked_solution:
Because the motion is undamped and the system experiences resonance, the forcing frequency equals the natural frequency $\omega .$

The external force is $f(t)=-12\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-3\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t),$ which is sinusoidal with frequency $3.$ Therefore,
$\omega =3.$

The complementary solution for the associated simple harmonic motion equation can be written in three different forms:

- ${y}_{c}=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(\omega t+ϕ)=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t+ϕ)$

- ${y}_{c}=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(\omega t+ϕ)=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t+ϕ)$

- ${y}_{c}=A\operatorname{cos}⁡\omega t+B\operatorname{sin}⁡\omega t=A\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)$

At resonance, a sinusoidal trial at frequency $\omega $ duplicates the complementary solution, so we multiply by $t$ and take a resonant particular solution of the form

$$
{y}_{p}(t)=t(C\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+D\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)).
$$

By substituting the particular solution and $\omega =3$ into the differential equation, ${y}^{″}+{\omega }^{2}y=f(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}[(6D-9Ct)\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-(6C+9Dt)\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)]+9t(C\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+D\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)) & =-12\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-3\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t) \\ 6D\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-6C\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t) & =-12\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-3\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)\end{aligned}
$$

Equating coefficients, $C=\frac{1}{2}$ and $D=-2.$ 

So, the particular solution is

$$
{y}_{p}(t)=\frac{1}{2}t\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-2t\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t).
$$

Finally, then, the general solution is given by the sum of the complementary and particular solutions. So, it can be written in any of the following forms:

- $y=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t+ϕ)+\frac{1}{2}t\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-2t\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)$

- $y=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t+ϕ)+\frac{1}{2}t\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-2t\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)$

- $y=A\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)+\frac{1}{2}t\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-2t\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)$

Solutions I, II, and III match the forms above.
Therefore, the correct answer is "I, II, and III".

- $y=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t+ϕ)+\frac{5}{8}t\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)$
- $y=A\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)-\frac{5}{8}t\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)$

Note that $A,$ $B,$ $R,$ and $ϕ$ are constants.
questions.worked_solution:
Because the motion is undamped and the system experiences resonance, the forcing frequency equals the natural frequency $\omega .$

The external force is $f(t)=5\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t),$ which is sinusoidal with frequency $4.$ Therefore,
$\omega =4.$

The complementary solution for the associated simple harmonic motion equation can be written in three different forms:

- ${y}_{c}=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(\omega t+ϕ)=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t+ϕ)$

- ${y}_{c}=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(\omega t+ϕ)=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t+ϕ)$

- ${y}_{c}=A\operatorname{cos}⁡\omega t+B\operatorname{sin}⁡\omega t=A\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)$

At resonance, a sinusoidal trial at frequency $\omega $ duplicates the complementary solution, so we multiply by $t$ and take a resonant particular solution of the form

$$
{y}_{p}(t)=t(C\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)+D\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)).
$$

By substituting the particular solution and $\omega =4$ into the differential equation, ${y}^{″}+{\omega }^{2}y=f(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}[16(D-Ct)\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)-16(C+Dt)\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)]+16t(C\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)+D\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)) & =5\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t) \\ 16D\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)-16C\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t) & =5\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)\end{aligned}
$$

Equating coefficients, $C=0$ and $D=\frac{5}{8}.$ 

So, the particular solution is

$$
{y}_{p}(t)=\frac{5}{8}t\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t).
$$

Finally, then, the general solution is given by the sum of the complementary and particular solutions. So, it can be written in any of the following forms:

- $y=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t+ϕ)+\frac{5}{8}t\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)$

- $y=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t+ϕ)+\frac{5}{8}t\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)$

- $y=A\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)+\frac{5}{8}t\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)$

Only solution II matches the forms above.
Therefore, the correct answer is "II only".

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Value of a Parameter that Results in Resonance
canonical_examples.problem:
The position $y(t),$ measured in meters, of a particle oscillating with periodically forced harmonic motion without damping is governed by the equation

$$
y'' + 25y =2\sin^2{pt},
$$

where $t > 0$ is the time, in seconds. Which value of the parameter $p$ causes the oscillator to resonate?
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we find the general solution of the differential equation. The complementary solution $y_c$ here represents simple harmonic motion, and it can be written as

$$
y_c=A\cos{\omega t} + B\sin{\omega t}.
$$

In our case,

$$
\omega^2 = 25\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \omega = 5,
$$

so, we have

$$
y_c=A\cos{5 t} + B\sin{5 t}.
$$

The oscillator experiences resonance when the frequency of the external periodic force $2 \sin^2 pt$ is equal to the frequency of the complementary solution, which is $\omega = 5.$ Since

$$
f(t) = 2 \sin^2 pt = 1 - \cos 2pt,
$$

the frequency of the external periodic force is $2p.$ Therefore, the oscillator experiences resonance when

$$
2p = 5 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad p = \dfrac{5}{2}.
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Determining the Spring Constant Given an External Periodic Force
canonical_examples.problem:
A particle of mass $0.25\,\textrm{kg}$ is attached to a massless spring. An external periodic force $F(t) = 3\sin(6t)\,\textrm{N}$ is applied to the particle.

The position of the particle is $y(t)$ (measured in meters), and $t>0$ is the time in seconds. If the particle moves with forced harmonic motion without damping and the system experiences resonance, what is the spring constant $k?$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The equation of motion for a particle of mass $m$ moving with forced harmonic motion without damping under the action of a spring with spring constant $k$ and external force $F(t)$ is given by

$$
my'' = -ky + F(t).
$$

Substituting our values for $m$ and $F(t)$ gives

$$
0.25y'' = - ky + 3\sin(6t).
$$

Simplifying and rearranging the above equation, we get

$$
y'' + 4ky = 12\sin(6t).
$$

The complementary solution $y_c$ here represents simple harmonic motion, and it can be written as

$$
y_c = A\cos \omega t + B\sin \omega t,
$$

where $A$ and $B$ are arbitrary constants of integration, and $\omega$ is the system's internal frequency.

In our case,

$$
\omega^2 = 4k
\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
k = \dfrac14\omega^2.
$$

The oscillator experiences resonance when the frequency of the external periodic force $f(t)=12\sin(6t),$ which is $6,$ is equal to the frequency of the complementary solution $\omega.$

Therefore,

$$
k = \dfrac14\omega^2 = \dfrac14\cdot6^2 = 9 \,\textrm{kg/s}^2.
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Identifying Solutions to Forced Harmonic Motion Equations
canonical_examples.problem:
A particle is moving with forced harmonic motion without damping. The particle is acted on by an external periodic force
$f(t) = 4\cos(4t)+12\sin(4t).$
Assuming the system experiences resonance, which of the following could be used to represent the general solution for the position $y(t)?$

- $y = R\cos(4t+\phi) - \dfrac{3}{2}t\cos(4t) + \dfrac{1}{2}t\sin(4t)$

- $y = R\sin(4t+\phi) - \dfrac{3}{2}t\cos(4t) + \dfrac{1}{2}t\sin(4t)$

- $y = A\cos(4t) + B\sin(4t) - \dfrac{3}{2}t\cos(4t)$

Note that $A,$ $B,$ $R,$ and $\phi$ are constants.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Because the motion is undamped and the system experiences resonance, the forcing frequency equals the natural frequency $\omega.$

The external force is $f(t)=4\cos(4t)+12\sin(4t),$ which is sinusoidal with frequency $4.$ Therefore,
$\omega = 4.$

The complementary solution for the associated simple harmonic motion equation can be written in three different forms:

- $y_c = R\cos{(\omega t + \phi)} = R\cos{(4t + \phi)}$

- $y_c = R\sin{(\omega t + \phi)} = R\sin{(4t + \phi)}$

- $y_c =A\cos{\omega t} + B\sin{\omega t} = A\cos(4t) + B\sin(4t)$

At resonance, a sinusoidal trial at frequency $\omega$ duplicates the complementary solution, so we multiply by $t$ and take a resonant particular solution of the form

$$
y_p(t)=t(C\cos(4t)+D\sin(4t)).
$$

By substituting the particular solution and $\omega=4$ into the differential equation, $y'' + \omega^2y = f(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}[8(D-2Ct)\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)-8(C+2Dt)\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)]+16t(C\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)+D\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)) & =4\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)+12\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t) \\ 8D\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)-8C\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t) & =4\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)+12\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)\end{aligned}
$$

Equating coefficients, $C=-\dfrac{3}{2}$ and $D=\dfrac{1}{2}.$ 

So, the particular solution is

$$
y_p(t) = -\dfrac{3}{2}t\cos(4t) + \dfrac{1}{2}t\sin(4t).
$$

Finally, then, the general solution is given by the sum of the complementary and particular solutions. So, it can be written in any of the following forms:

- $y = R\cos{(4t + \phi)} - \dfrac{3}{2}t\cos(4t) + \dfrac{1}{2}t\sin(4t)$

- $y = R\sin{(4t + \phi)} - \dfrac{3}{2}t\cos(4t) + \dfrac{1}{2}t\sin(4t)$

- $y = A\cos(4t) + B\sin(4t) - \dfrac{3}{2}t\cos(4t) + \dfrac{1}{2}t\sin(4t)$

Only solutions I and II match the forms above. Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only".
